newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mancera argues against sliding Mexico peso policy.
newsitem.headline: Mancera argues against sliding Mexico peso policy.

text.p: Banco de Mexico Governor Miguel Mancera said Thursday the argument than an undervalued exchange rate fosters growth was not persuasive.

"In the medium and long term, the international competitiveness of Mexican products cannot be founded on the perpetural devaluation of the exchange rate," Mancera said in prepared remarks to a closed-door meeting sponsored by The Economist magazine.
He noted that some sectors of society have been concerned about the relative stability of the exchange rate this year, seeing it as an obstacle to economic recovery.
But he said while some groups benefit from an undervalued peso, others suffer, real wages remain depressed and inflation and interest rate pressures rise.
"The idea that a permanently undervalued exchange rate fosters economic growth, or that it is beneficial to all, is not persuasive," Mancera said.

"It must also be emphasized that the current monetary and exchange rate policies are in no way designed to forestall the depreciation of the domestic currency, should the fundamental conditions of the economy so warrant," he added.
